cosy-lesson.title: Fit Hot Guys Have Problems Too

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Shallow – Lacking depth of intellect, emotion, or seriousness.

p.em: Example: The song parodies male models complaining about trivial problems with absurd seriousness.

cosy-blockquote.p: Privilege – A special right, advantage, or immunity granted to a particular person or group.

p.em: Example: They whine about handsome privilege while strutting around in a boyband routine.

cosy-blockquote.p: Superficial – Existing or occurring at or on the surface; not thorough or deep.

p.em: Example: Complaining that your abs are too defined is the definition of a superficial problem.

cosy-blockquote.p: Absurd – Wildly unreasonable, illogical, or ridiculous.

p.em: Example: Watching three gorgeous guys cry over trivial minor inconveniences is absurd.

cosy-blockquote.p: Sympathy – Feelings of pity and sorrow for someone else's misfortune.

p.em: Example: They demand deep sympathy from the audience for problems nobody cares about.

cosy-blockquote.p: Symmetric – Made up of exactly similar parts facing each other on an axis.

p.em: Example: Having a perfectly symmetric face apparently carries immense emotional weight.

cosy-blockquote.p: Boyband – A pop group composed of young attractive men, performing synchronized routines.

p.em: Example: The song parodies classic late 90s boyband dance moves and dramatic emotional poses.

cosy-blockquote.p: Trivial – Of little value or importance.

p.em: Example: Confusing a genuinely hard life with trivial aesthetic problems is hilarious satire.

cosy-blockquote.p: Validation – Recognition or affirmation that a person or their feelings are valid.

p.em: Example: Even incredibly attractive people crave constant external validation.

cosy-blockquote.p: Glamour – An attractive or exciting quality that makes certain people seem appealing.

p.em: Example: The glamour of being ridiculously hot comes with unexpected comedic downside.
